summary: The Leon Ve is the only plug-in hybrid Leon hatch sold in Australia, a detuned 150kW version of the Volkswagen Group's second-generation 1.5-litre eHybrid with a 19.7kWh usable battery and 123km of claimed electric range, priced at $62,990 before on-road costs since its mid-2026 launch. No Australian outlet has yet published a full review of the hatch, so the verdict leans on the mechanically related Leon Sportstourer VZe wagon, which CarExpert and Chasing Cars praised for 'outstanding' plugged-in efficiency and a fun chassis but marked down for road noise and a price north of $70,000. The hatch body is the catch: the battery shrinks the boot to 270 litres, and the 200kW VZe plug-in is offered here only as the Sportstourer wagon, which this dataset does not list.
pros: 123km of claimed electric range (Cupra Australia's figure; Europe's WLTP rating on the same 18-inch tyre is 131km) from a 19.7kWh usable battery outlasts the Formentor VZe's 114km and almost doubles the Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV's 86km
At $62,990 before on-road costs it is the cheapest way into the Volkswagen Group's long-range eHybrid in Australia, $6,000 under the Cupra Formentor VZe and $1,600 under the VW Tiguan 150TSI eHybrid
50kW DC fast charging (10-80 per cent in about 26 minutes) and an 11kW onboard AC charger, up from 3.6kW on the previous Leon plug-in, which few small plug-in hybrids match
1.4L/100km and 33g/km CO2 on the label clear the 3.5L/100km fuel-efficient LCT test and Victoria's 120g/km green-car duty threshold, and the price sits well under the $75,000 FBT cap

Five-year unlimited-kilometre warranty, with the high-voltage battery covered for 8 years/160,000km; Cupra's November-December 2026 offer adds a $5,850 cashback on MY25 and MY26 Leons ordered and delivered by 31 December
cons: The battery cuts the boot to 270 litres to the window line (ADAC: 270 to 1,191 litres to the roof), against the 344 litres Cupra Australia quotes for the Leon range, which is less than many city hatches

Once the battery is flat it is a 1,673kg hatch on a 1.5-litre engine: ADAC's WLTP battery-empty figure is 5.1L/100km from a 40-litre tank, and Chasing Cars saw consumption head towards 6L/100km on a low battery in the related VZe wagon, so the case depends on home charging

No Australian braked tow rating is published for the Ve hatch, and Germany's ADAC lists the 150kW Leon eHybrid hatch with no approved trailer load; buyers who need to tow should look at the 1,700kg-rated Sportstourer VZe wagon
It gives up 50kW to the Formentor and Terramar VZe on the same drivetrain (150kW/350Nm, 7.7sec to 100km/h), and reviewers of the related wagon flagged intrusive road noise

Plug-in hybrids lost the FBT exemption on 1 April 2025, there is no dedicated Australian review of the hatch yet, and Cupra's history of deep run-out discounting on earlier Leon and Formentor plug-ins makes resale a risk
